subject: Post-call readout: executive alignment, risks, and procurement next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novamed.com>, Mark Davis <mark.davis@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call readout: executive alignment, risks, and procurement next steps

Hi Laura / Mark —

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick readout for your exec team and a proposed close path so we all have the same playbook. I captured the key business outcomes, the risks you flagged, and concrete next steps for procurement/legal to move a pilot forward.

What you told us (concise):
- Business outcomes: 40–60% reduction in triage time for clinical notes ingestion; improve discharge summarization accuracy (reduce manual edits by ~30%); measurable uplift in clinician satisfaction scores.
- Primary constraints: sub-200ms tail latency on inference for interactive workflows, strict PHI controls, and an auditable log retention policy for 12+ months.
- Secondary asks: cost predictability for pilot, ability to fall back to a smaller model for high-throughput batch jobs, and SOC 2 readiness evidence.

Top risks (and our mitigations):
1) Data residency / PHI concerns — we recommended Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed keys; Jasmine will outline the KMS/HSM integration in the tech appendix.
2) Latency SLO — runtime-level continuous batching and prefix caching; we propose a latency SLA for the pilot with staged thresholds and automatic fallback to lower-cost variants.
3) Contract timing — procurement expects a 6–8 week legal review; we'll provide a focused pilot SOW + templated Data Processing Addendum to shorten review.

Proposed pilot (4 weeks):
- Scope: Inference on anonymized clinical notes, integration via our hosted private endpoint, dataset size ~100k docs, 2 daily peak windows simulated.
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency <= 200ms for interactive calls; end-to-end accuracy delta vs current baseline >= +15% on extractive tasks; cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold.
- Deliverables: onboarding runbook, dashboard access, weekly syncs, and a final handoff playbook for production rollout.

Attachments: NDA_Redwood_v1.pdf (for your legal), pilot_scope_novamed.xlsx (scope + costs).

Requested next steps (simple playbook):
1) Laura: confirm decision authority and preferred procurement contact (name + email).
2) Mark / Procurement: indicate any non-standard contract clauses to surface early.
3) Legal: review attached NDA (I can provide a redline-friendly version in DocuSign).
4) Redwood: Jasmine will send the tech appendix and a preliminary pilot runbook by Monday; Ben will scope commercial options (pilot pricing + exec discount cadence).

If that aligns, I’ll trigger the NDA + pilot SOW and schedule a kickoff for the week of May 10.

Thanks — short and actionable is the goal here.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0148

Grace —

Appreciate the concise summary. This matches what we heard in the meeting. A few clarifications from our side before we loop procurement:

1) Decision authority: I'm the exec sponsor for product/clinical, Mark is the fiscal approver. Final contract sig will come from our CFO (Mark) or delegated authority; I will confirm delegation by Monday.
2) Procurement contact: Please include our procurement lead, Elena Torres (procurement@novamed.com). She will triage legal and purchasing.
3) Legal asks: we have two standing items — (a) limitation of liability cap tied to annual run rate (not per-pilot), and (b) clarification on log retention/erase requests for patient-identifiable data. We'll start an internal redline and share within 5 business days.
4) Timeline: if legal/procurement can turn in ~10 business days, the pilot kickoff the week of May 17 is feasible. If reviews take longer, we may push to early June.

Please proceed with the NDA and pilot SOW. Also, could you include a short note in the SOW about our ability to opt for a private deployment variant if we decide to broaden scope after the pilot? That will help our InfoSec signoff.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Chen

Grace / team —

Good readout. A couple commercial notes to help unblock procurement quickly:
- Pilot pricing: I will propose a fixed-cost pilot option (limited-duration license) to avoid per-token uncertainty; will put numbers in HubSpot by Monday.
- Executive concession path: if NovaMed commits to a production rollout within 90 days after pilot and meets a committed spend threshold, we can convert a portion of pilot fees into a production credit. I will mark that clause in our playbook.
- Contract escrows / liability: we can accept a liability cap tied to the pilot value for the SOW; for enterprise contract terms we will need standard legal review.

Internal asks for Jasmine / Marissa:
1) Jasmine — prepare a 1-page tech appendix focused on KMS/HSM options and the private deployment checklist.
2) Marissa — schedule a 30-minute intro between Elena (procurement) and our legal counsel. Please include the SOW draft and the NDA redline.

I'll be available if execs want a short call with me next week.
